$comment: Motion library catalog. Read this when matching a scene's spoken words to a motion template. Each entry has a name (used in scenes.json motion field), a summary, the keywords/themes that should trigger it, and any optional props the agent can pass to customize.

templates.name: ChartConvergence
templates.summary: Two opposing market bar strips slide in from L/R, meet at center, gold arrow rises out of the convergence.
templates.use_when: transcript mentions matching, arbitrage, opportunity, opposing forces, convergence, two sides meeting, balance, equilibrium, deal closing

props_optional.name: leftBars
props_optional.description: 8 normalized heights (0..1) for the left chart

props_optional.name: rightBars
props_optional.description: 8 normalized heights (0..1) for the right chart

templates.name: Timeline
templates.summary: Horizontal track draws across, milestone markers pop in staggered with year labels.
templates.use_when: transcript mentions experience, history, journey, evolution, year-by-year, track record, growth over time, milestones, before/after sequencing

props_optional.name: milestones
props_optional.type: Array<{ x: number, popFrame: number, label: string, sub?: string }>
props_optional.description: Override the default 4 milestones. x is in 1080-wide coords, popFrame is when it appears.

templates.name: ProblemSolution
templates.summary: Tangled scribble on left fades, clean target+arrow springs in on right, gold arrow bridges them.
templates.use_when: transcript mentions defining a problem, finding a solution, before/after, chaos to clarity, fix, breakthrough, solve, untangle, debug, refactor, simplify

templates.name: BrowserBuilds
templates.summary: Browser window chrome assembles, then UI components fade in (header, sidebar, content card with chart, action button).
templates.use_when: transcript mentions building a web app, shipping a product, deploying, dashboard, software, web interface, prototype, MVP, launching

templates.name: ClockProgress
templates.summary: Analog clock face with sweeping second hand, progress bar at 95%, pulsing notification dot. Calm pacing.
templates.use_when: transcript mentions waiting, paused, anticipation, time passing, almost done, pending, in-progress, queued, deliberate, slow, hold

templates.name: TierStack
templates.summary: Stacked chat-bubble cards at ascending Y positions, each more elaborate than the one below (1 line → 3 lines → with chart → with code).
templates.use_when: transcript mentions scope, capability, tiers, levels, scale, altitude, what's possible, sophistication, depth, ladder, range of options

props_optional.name: codeSnippet
props_optional.description: Override the line of code in the top bubble

templates.name: KineticType
templates.summary: Full-bleed kinetic typography. Words pop in stagger with overshoot rotation, last word colored in accent. No surrounding card. Different layout family from the cards-and-charts entries.
templates.use_when: transcript hits an emphatic, declarative line: payoff, mantra, punchline, 'the truth is...', 'saves you mad time', 'don't sleep on this', single bold statement

props_optional.name: text
props_optional.description: The line to render. Will be split on whitespace and rendered word-per-line. ALL CAPS reads best.

props_optional.name: bg
props_optional.description: Background. Default 'navy'. 'paper' for instructional tone, 'none' to layer over previous content.

props_optional.name: highlightIndex
props_optional.description: Which word index gets accent color. Defaults to last word.

templates.name: TerminalCommand
templates.summary: Dark terminal-style background with scanlines. Types a command char-by-char after a `$` prompt, then streams 2-4 output lines below with a blinking cursor. Different background and font from every other library entry.
templates.use_when: transcript mentions code, commands, technical execution, 'run this', 'call the function', CLI flavor, anything that benefits from a monospace/code aesthetic

props_optional.name: output
props_optional.description: Output lines streamed under the command. Lines starting with ✓ render green, ✗ red, → accent.

templates.name: SplitWipe
templates.summary: True split-screen: muted maroon left half (failure) vs deep teal right half (success), with halves sliding in from opposite edges, then a glowing accent divider, then big ✕/✓ glyphs and labels. Replaces ProblemSolution when the contrast needs to be sharper.
templates.use_when: transcript hits before/after, vs, then/now, A/B comparison, two paths, 'here's what happens without it', 'here's what happens with it'. Stronger than ProblemSolution when the user wants a hard visual divider.

templates.name: NetworkNodes
templates.summary: Blueprint-grid background with 7 asymmetrically scattered nodes that drift via deterministic noise. Edges draw on between them via stroke-dashoffset. One 'hot' node pulses in accent. Asymmetric layout — label is top-left, badge is bottom-right.
templates.use_when: transcript mentions connections, ecosystem, network, 'everyone is using it', users, 'all of this is connected', graph, web of relationships, multi-party

matching_rules.$comment: How the agent should pick a template per scene
process: Read the scene's `words` field — what's actually said in this 4-second window
Look for keyword overlap with each template's `use_when` description
If multiple templates match, pick the one with the strongest/most specific match
If NOTHING matches well (score is low across the board), write a custom in src/broll-custom/ instead — do not force-fit a template
Write the chosen template name into the scene's `motion` field, e.g. `"motion": "Timeline"`
For customs, use the prefix `custom:` followed by the component name, e.g. `"motion": "custom:Scene07_OurStartup"`
